sentence: This project follows adolescents over time to study how social media use and mental health change and affect each other.
This project tries to find out how mitochondrial genotype, infection, mitochondrial function and tumorigenesis are linked in hepatocellular carcinoma among Hispanic people.
This project sets up a mass spectrometry system so researchers can analyze samples for work on substance use disorders and medication safety.
This project studies how the periplasmic flagella of spirochetes are assembled and how they help these bacteria move.
This project builds a platform that measures sickle hemoglobin polymer in single red blood cells to judge how well sickle cell anemia treatments work.
This project studies the neural mechanisms by which the cerebellum controls tongue movements in non-human primates.
This project studies how mild traumatic brain injury and changes in blood vessels of the brain relate to Alzheimer disease and neurodegenerative disease.
This project builds a model of ataxia telangiectasia using stem cells from patients to study how the disease affects cerebellar Purkinje cells.
This project tries to find out which protein networks drive regulated exocytosis.
This project studies whether pathogens of different species evolve the same drug resistance mutations and tries to find out why they differ.
This project tests which dose of radiation therapy works best with immunotherapy and chemotherapy in early-stage triple negative breast cancer.
This project builds tools based on ribosomes that measure how genes are controlled in very small numbers of specific neurons.
This project builds AI methods that read the genomes of microorganisms to predict how a microbiome changes over time.
This project uses electrophysiology and neural network modeling to study how brain pathways support coordination, integration and learning of movement.
This project tests whether piperlongumine, a natural product, and related compounds can protect against hearing loss in patients treated with antibiotics.
This project builds statistical machine learning methods that use baseline neuroimaging to better estimate treatment effects in clinical trials for Alzheimer's disease and late-life depression.
This project studies how resting brain activity changes in infants and toddlers and how it relates to brain structure and behavior.
This project uses single-molecule analyses to study how stereocilia of inner ear hair cells work, in order to find targets for treating hearing loss.
This project tries to find out how removing unfit cells from epithelia makes nearby stem cells produce new cells and keep cell numbers steady.
